description: This chapter deals with finding the total number of simple figures (like triangles, squares, rectangles) hidden inside complex geometric figures. It tests a student's visual observation and analytical ability.

sections.title: Counting of Straight Lines
sections.description: Counting the minimum straight lines required to form any polygon or complex figure.

key_concepts.explanation: Sleeping lines drawn from left to right.
Standing lines drawn from top to bottom.
Slanted lines drawn at an angle.

steps.title: Count Horizontal Lines
steps.detail: Consider all horizontal lines present in the figure as single lines from one end to the other and count them.

steps.title: Count Vertical Lines
steps.detail: Similarly, count all vertical lines in the figure.

steps.title: Count Slant Lines
steps.detail: Finally, count all the slanted or diagonal lines.

steps.title: Total Sum
steps.detail: Total straight lines = H + V + D

sections.title: Counting of Triangles - Basic Figures
sections.description: When a large triangle is divided into smaller parts vertically or horizontally.

equations: (where n = number of smaller triangles formed on the base)

results: Number the smaller triangles on the base as 1, 2, 3... and add them up (e.g., 1+2+3 = 6).
First find the number from the vertical division (n(n+1)/2), then multiply it by the total number of horizontal bases.

sections.title: Counting of Triangles - Inside Square/Rectangle
sections.description: When triangles are formed inside a quadrilateral, like a square or rectangle, by its diagonals.

equations: (where n = total number of small triangles connected to the center)

results: If a square is divided into 4 parts by both diagonals, total triangles = 4 * 2 = 8.
Count the triangles of both squares separately (8 + 8 = 16).
Then add the 2 large hidden triangles formed at their intersection/junction (Total = 18).

sections.title: Counting of Squares
sections.description: Finding the total number of squares in grid-like figures or chessboards.

cases.condition: When Rows and Columns are equal (Rows = Columns)
results: Sum the squares of numbers from 1 to n.

cases.condition: When Rows and Columns are unequal (m x n)
results: Continue this sequence until any one value becomes zero and then sum them up.

sections.title: Counting of Rectangles
sections.description: Finding the total number of rectangles in a given figure. Remember that every square is a rectangle, but every rectangle is not a square.

equations: Total Rectangles = (Sum of Rows) * (Sum of Columns)

steps.title: Number the Grid
steps.detail: Give numbers 1, 2, 3... to the rows and columns respectively.

steps.title: Sum of Rows
steps.detail: Add all the row numbers together.

steps.title: Sum of Columns
steps.detail: Add all the column numbers together.

steps.title: Multiply
steps.detail: Multiply both sums to get the total rectangles. If asked for 'Only Rectangles', subtract the total squares from the total rectangles.
